subject.title: Approvals lost on gateway restart — stale callback buttons show confusing error

question: Should pending exec/plugin approvals survive gateway restart, or should restart intentionally invalidate them fail-closed with clearer recovery across channels?
rationale: Current code and release behavior clear pending approvals on restart, while durable approval persistence changes the trust boundary for command/tool approval decisions and cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Fail closed with explicit recovery
options.body: Keep restart invalidation as the default, but make all channel surfaces clearly consume or replace stale approval UI and tell the user to re-request the action.

options.title: Persist pending approvals securely
options.body: Store pending approvals in SQLite with strict expiry, requester/reviewer binding, replay protection, and restart/live proof before accepting stale buttons after restart.

options.title: Split by approval kind
options.body: Persist only lower-risk plugin approvals while continuing to invalidate exec approvals on restart, with docs/tests explaining the security boundary.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with explicit recovery
recommendation.body: Keep restart invalidation as the default, but make all channel surfaces clearly consume or replace stale approval UI and tell the user to re-request the action.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the shared gateway approval helpers and is the strongest history signal for the core approval trust boundary in this review.
